I've read that ketogenic diets have some anti-inflammatory effects (or rather, that carbs tend to have inflammatory effects). I was wondering how strong this is? On one end of the spectrum is fish oil, which I believes improves inflammation markers in the blood, but doesn't actually seem to reduce or cure any inflammation related injuries. On the other end is prescription strength NSAIDs (or possibly steroids), which will take an injury like mine down a notch but have the lovely side effect of heart attack and stroke (or destroying your connective tissues, for steroids).

So how strong is the anti-inflammatory effect of this dietary change? Is the change nil if my former diet didn't have too much sugar? Has this been studied, or have any athletes noticed a difference in minor joint injuries?
Do keto diets have a *strong* anti-inflammatory effect?

I don't think there is anything which can scientifically answer your question. Simply put, ketogenic diets are not all that well researched outside of particular applications in treating epilepsy, less so for general weight loss, and even less so some protection/treatment against Alzheimer's. Regarding inflammation in general (which can have multiple sources), I don't think there has been many attempts to even investigate. Most claims are (as you said) based simply on the fact that carbohydrates are inherently inflammatory and a ketogenic diet reduces them. I believe the general consensus would be that a ketogenic diet (high in w-3 and low in vegetable oils) can be effective for certain responsive individuals but not necessarily for general populations.

Really, the best advice is to consult with your doctor. State your intention and bring print-outs of supporting evidence of the anti-inflammatory effects of your diet (preferably reports directly from studies). The fact is, most doctors don't have a whole lot of training on nutrition (being that there are so many maladies they have to learn how to treat, specifically). Armed with that discussion and following observations, you can fine-tune your prescriptions. If your just taking over-the-counter medicine, you may have to find the proper balance on your own through reducing dosage to threshold levels of discomfort and observing the effects. If it helps, I've heard it said that suffering is good for the soul.

I have joint injuries all over the damn place, and can tell you that keto is weakly anti-inflammatory for that to me. I was really hoping that it would be better. It's all about omega 3 to me, and NSAIDs when things get unbearably bad.

1. BHB has been shown to have an anti-inflammatory effect. To what extent, I don't know.
  2. Even if your diet is devoid of sugar, any carbs eaten will increase inflammation via release of ROS from carb metabolism.
  3. Aspirin is a better option than NSAIDS
  4. I take hyaluronic acid + MSM for my joints
